reason: E3 demonstrates reactive wear protection via an in-situ oxide nanocomposite in TiNbZr-Ag, supporting the glaze-layer concept, but it does not involve CoCrFeNi or a minor reactive additive. E1 shows tribochemical carbon film formation catalyzed by HEA nanoflakes, not oxide glaze from a matrix additive. The cited evidence does not directly support the specific claim that a minor reactive element in CoCrFeNi will form a lubricious oxide glaze across the full temperature range.
premises: Reactive element addition promotes controlled tribo-oxidation in CoCrFeNi
Tribo-oxidation forms an adaptive, lubricious oxide nanocomposite (glaze) layer
The glaze layer reduces friction and wear from RT to 800 °C
The glaze layer is continuously regenerated during sliding
The mechanism is analogous to reactive wear protection in TiNbZr-Ag
